description: Born in 1924, surrealism wants to liberate the unconscious: dreams, desires, crazy associations. **Dalí** delirium, **Magritte** enigmatizes.

hero.hook: What if reason was a prison, and dreams were the only way out?

blocks.text: **surrealism** (1924-1969) is not just a style: it is a revolution in thought. After the First World War, he wanted to merge dream and consciousness, where reality and imagination ceased to oppose each other.
With **Salvador Dalí** and **René Magritte**, the movement invents a global visual grammar. One plunges into personal delirium; the other in the cold and philosophical enigma.

The poet **André Breton** founded the movement with the *Surrealism Manifesto* in **1924**. After the [[Dadaism]], which destroyed meaning, Breton wants to rebuild the mind by freeing thought. He speaks of “pure psychic automatism”: writing or painting without control of reason.

blocks.caption: The Manifesto of 1924: surrealism becomes a program.

blocks.text: Breton collected “primitive” art objects and curiosities. When he died, his workshop contained more than 5,000 pieces intended to stimulate the imagination.

The inspiration comes from the [[Freudian psychoanalysis as a source]]: Sigmund Freud shows that the unconscious dominates the psyche. To circumvent internal censorship, the surrealists invented and, this game where everyone adds a sentence or a drawing without seeing the previous one. The goal: to paint the unreal with a disturbing realism, to make people doubt the stable world. [[Automatic writing]] [[Exquisite Corpse]]

The Catalan **Salvador Dalí** (1904-1989) joined the group in **1929**. He invented the “paranoid-critical” method: a voluntary delirium where he combines heterogeneous elements. His phobias become universal symbols.

blocks.caption: The Persistence of Memory: Time That Melts.

blocks.text: Dalí was terrified of grasshoppers since childhood. He associates them in his paintings with the fear of time passing and death.

*The Persistence of Memory* (**1931**) shows soft watches in a -inspired landscape on the Catalan coast. Breton nicknamed it “Avida Dollars” and excluded it in **1939**. But Dalí had already transformed surrealism into a global phenomenon, served by a technique worthy of the Renaissance. [[Port Lligat]]

The Belgian **René Magritte** (1898-1967) led an ordinary life and often painted in his dining room. His surrealism is not dreamlike: it is intellectual. It reveals the mystery hidden in everyday life through visual paradoxes.

blocks.caption: “This is not a pipe”: the image is not the thing.

blocks.text: *The Betrayal of Images* (**1929**) writes under a perfect pipe: “This is not a pipe”. The image is a sign, not the object. Bowler hat, apple, clouds: Magritte creates enigmas. We sometimes talk about : the strange is born from a slightly distorted familiar world. [[Magical realism]]
Before making a living from his painting, Magritte designed wallpaper and advertisements for Belgian fashion houses: hence his taste for repetition and order.

sections.title: Magritte: the mystery of everyday life

blocks.text: Surrealism permeates cinema, fashion and our visual culture. After **1924**, art no longer has the obligation to copy the outside world: it can delve into the most obscure intimacy.

events.detail: Two paths: controlled delirium and philosophical enigma.
events.title: Dalí and Magritte

events.detail: Soft watches become a global icon.
events.title: The Persistence of Memory

blocks.text: Dalí pushes self-expression to the point of extravagance; Magritte questions the truth of images and announces conceptual art. The movement formally died out with Breton in **1966**, but its legacy remains.
Surrealism frees the unconscious from the control of reason. Dalí invents paranoia-critique; Magritte transforms the everyday image into a philosophical enigma.
